title: Numerical Investigation of Pulverized Coal–Hydrogen Co-Injection in a Pressurized Reactor: Fixed-Carbon Conversion, Particle Residence Time, and Oxygen Availability
content: A transient Eulerian–Lagrangian framework was used to investigate pulverized coal injection (PCI) with four nominal hydrogen loadings in a pressurized reactor inspired by laboratory experiments at UFOP. OpenFOAM Foundation v13 resolved compressible multicomponent gas flow, global irreversible hydrogen oxidation, reacting coal parcels, heterogeneous char oxidation, and CO₂ gasification. The oxygen molar feed and injected PCI mass were fixed, while hydrogen addition altered gas flow, composition, and velocity. Four equal PCI pulses were injected during a 30 ms observation period. Predicted fixed-carbon conversion decreased from 90.48% without hydrogen to 89.55%, 83.60%, and 67.94% at hydrogen loadings of 5, 10, and 20 kg per tonne of hot metal, respectively. Previous UFOP experiments provide a physical reference, although differing performance indicators and operating conditions prevent direct quantitative validation. Mean observed residence times of exported parcels decreased from 12.39 ms without hydrogen to 8.53, 6.96, and 5.39 ms, respectively. Fixed-carbon inventory accounting closed in all cases, with a maximum absolute residual of 1.52 × 10⁻¹⁹ kg. The conversion trend cannot be attributed solely to residence time because oxygen availability and thermal conditions also varied. These findings characterize coupled transport and reaction effects within the specified numerical configuration and highlight limitations of simplified reactive-flow modeling.
